analysis.title: Murphy Oil Corp. (MUR): First Take: 3Q26 EBITDAX Beat Versus Consensus; Focus on Outlook for Bubale Appraisal Program
key_insights: MUR reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $1.08 and adjusted EBITDAX of $544 mn, against FactSet consensus of $0.91 and $507 mn and GS estimates of $0.60 and $501 mn.
3Q26 oil production was 84 Mbo/d and total production was 186 Mboe/d, versus GS estimates of 80 and 179 and consensus of 81 and 179.
3Q26 capex was $422 mn, below GS ($429 mn) and consensus ($426 mn). Free cash flow was $93 mn versus GS $89 mn and consensus $51 mn. Net debt was $1.13 bn versus GS $1.07 bn and consensus $1.06 bn.
MUR returned $50 mn to shareholders through dividends in the quarter.

4Q26 guidance: total production ex-non-controlling interest of 174-182 Mboe/d (GS and consensus 176), oil production of ~83 Mbo/d (GS 89, consensus 87), and capex of $190 mn (GS $254 mn, consensus $223 mn). Oil guidance and capex are below both estimates.

2026 guidance: total production ex-non-controlling interest raised to 176-178 Mboe/d from 167-175 Mboe/d (GS and consensus 175). Oil guidance lowered to ~85 Mbo/d from ~86 Mbo/d (GS 86, consensus 85). Capex held at $1.50-$1.60 bn.

International: after 3Q26 MUR signed agreements with Mauritania for two offshore exploration blocks. Lac Da Vang reached first oil late in 3Q26 and is expected to ramp to 3-5 Mboe/d in FY2027. Hai Su Vang FID remains on track for late 2027. A Cameroon agreement is expected by YE2026.
Other: MUR secured 6 exploration blocks in the August Gulf of America lease sale and began production at the Chinook #8 development well in the Gulf of America.
GS rates MUR Neutral with a 12-month price target of $44 against a $35.94 close on 4 Nov 2026, implying 22.4% upside. M&A rank is 2.

The price target is a 50/50 blend of DCF ($44) and FCF yield. The FCF yield leg uses a 6.0% target yield on 2027/2028 estimates at $80/$75 Brent and $3.50 Henry Hub, with 42.5% weight on a ~$40 fundamental value and 7.5% on a ~$65 M&A value.
GS's key questions for the 9 AM ET call: the Bubale appraisal program through 2027, Hai Su Vang FID outlook, the Eagle Ford activity ramp, A&D opportunities, and the Cameroon and Mauritania strategy.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral with a $44 target after the 3Q26 beat. The target was raised from $36 on 26-Oct-26. The M&A rank of 2 adds a theoretical value of ~$65 at 7.5% weight.

earnings_insights: MUR 3Q26 adjusted EPS reported $1.08 vs FactSet consensus $0.91 and GS estimate $0.60. Adjusted EBITDAX reported $544 mn vs consensus $507 mn and GS $501 mn (adjusted for non-controlling interests).
3Q26 operating cash flow reported $515 mn vs GS $518 mn and consensus $477 mn. Cash flow per share was $3.53 vs GS $3.54 and consensus $3.30.
3Q26 realized prices: oil $89.35/bbl vs GS $85.22, gas $1.84/Mcf vs GS $1.68, NGLs $23.08/bbl vs GS $23.26. Total cash costs were $14.19/BOE vs GS $14.18.
4Q26 guidance: capex of $190 mn vs GS $254 mn and consensus $223 mn. Oil production of ~83 Mbo/d vs GS 89 and consensus 87.
FY2026 guidance: total production 176-178 Mboe/d (raised from 167-175), oil ~85 Mbo/d (lowered from ~86), capex $1.50-$1.60 bn (maintained).
GS forecasts (estimates, not reported): FY26E EPS $4.48, FY27E $3.65, FY28E $3.31. Quarterly EPS estimates are $0.60 for 9/26E, $1.98 for 12/26E and $0.87 for 3/27E. Reported 6/26 EPS was $1.58.
risk_factors: GS names costs, well results, commodity price volatility and government pronouncements as key risks.
geopolitical: MUR signed agreements with the government of Mauritania for two offshore exploration blocks.
MUR expects to finalize an agreement in Cameroon by YE2026.
